Merman Construction's Quality Commitment
As a small family-owned business, Merman Construction takes pride in helping Montgomery and Chester County homeowners transform their spaces with additions and home remodeling projects. Steve Merman and his team treat every project like their own, bringing trusted craftsmanship, integrity, and careful attention to every detail.

Select one of the services below to learn more.
	
Home Additions

Primary suites, in-law suites, garages, and custom expansions for homes across Montgomery and Chester Counties. We use materials like Aquaguard® performance laminate flooring and engineered structural framing to ensure safe, long-lasting additions.

	
Stucco Remediation

Full removal and repair with James Hardie® siding, stone, or vinyl replacement to protect your exterior. We use Benjamin Opdyke HydroGap® drainable house wrap and HydroFlash® GP.

	
Windows & Doors

Energy efficient window replacements and premium entry doors that improve comfort, security, and home value. Brands such as ViWinco® Windows and Reeb® Doors are used.

	
Basements

Entertainment rooms, home gyms, playrooms, or in-law apartments, tailored to your property. Quality materials such as Diamond Cabinets and Sherwin-Williams paint.

	
Siding & Exterior

Expert installation of James Hardie®  fiber cement siding and Certainteed® vinyl siding to boost curb appeal and weather resistance.

	
Deck Installation

Built with Trex® and AZEK® composite materials for long lasting decks, porches, and pergolas.

	
Bathrooms & Kitchens

Beautifully finished kitchens and bathrooms designed for comfort and function. Quality materials from Kohler and Ferguson Plumbing Supply.

9
	
Craftmanship

We are a family-owned remodeling company that takes pride in traditional craftsmanship while applying modern building practices. Every project is built with precision, care, and long-lasting results.

9
	
Compliance

Merman Construction ensures that every home renovation complies with all local building codes and safety standards, giving homeowners confidence in both quality and reliability.

Serving Montgomery County & Chester County, PA

Our goal is simple: deliver expert craftsmanship and dependable service that homeowners can trust for lasting results. From home additions and stucco remediation to decks, bathroom remodels, and full home renovations, we bring the same level of planning and precision to every project.

Professional Home Remodeling and Stucco Remediation in Montgomery and Chester County

 

Merman Construction Inc provides professional home remodeling services for homeowners across Montgomery and Chester Counties. Our team specializes in home additions, basement finishing, kitchen and bathroom renovations, deck construction, and stucco remediation.

With more than 20 years of experience, we are a family owned contractor trusted throughout Collegeville, Phoenixville, Royersford, Plymouth Meeting, and nearby communities. Every project is built with lasting craftsmanship, personalized design, and a commitment to quality that adds comfort and value to your home.

ABOUT MERMAN CONSTRUCTION INC.

A Collegeville Construction Company Built on Trust, Craftsmanship, and Hands-On Experience

Merman Construction Inc. is a family-owned construction and remodeling company based in Collegeville, Pennsylvania. We work with homeowners throughout Montgomery and Chester County on larger residential projects, including home additions, stucco remediation, basement remodeling, exterior renovations, windows, doors, decks, and structural remodeling work.

VIEW OUR WORK
Start a Conversation
Why Homeowners Choose Merman Construction

A remodeling project is personal. Homeowners want to know who will be in their home, who is watching the details, and whether the company understands more than surface-level finish work.

Merman Construction is intentionally hands-on. Steve Merman began his career as a professional framer, building homes and residential developments throughout the region. That background still shapes the way we approach additions, exterior renovations, stucco remediation, basement projects, and larger remodeling work.

We look closely at how new work connects to the existing home. That includes framing, rooflines, siding transitions, window and door openings, water management, structure, permits, sequencing, and the details that affect how the project performs over time.

What This Means for Homeowners
Clearer planning before construction begins
Owner involvement throughout the project
Practical construction knowledge, not just sales talk
Respect for your home, schedule, and property
Attention to structure, exterior details, and water management
A More Thoughtful Approach to Remodeling
Craftsmanship

Merman Construction focuses on work that is built carefully, not rushed through. From framing and exterior details to finish selections and final walkthroughs, we pay attention to the parts of the project homeowners see every day and the parts they may never see behind the walls.

See examples in our remodeling portfolio.

Compliance

Larger remodeling projects often involve permits, inspections, township requirements, structural details, and documentation. Merman Construction helps homeowners understand what needs to happen before and during construction so the project can move forward with fewer surprises.

Learn more about planning for home additions in Montgomery and Chester County.

Serving Montgomery County & Chester County, PA

Based in Collegeville, Merman Construction works with homeowners throughout Montgomery and Chester County on larger residential construction and remodeling projects, including home additions, stucco remediation, basement remodeling, decks, exterior renovations, windows, and doors.

Explore our home additions, stucco remediation, and basement remodeling services.

YEARS ESTABLISHED

COMPLETED PROJECTS

 

About Steve Merman, Owner

Steve Merman is the Owner and Founder of Merman Construction Inc., a home remodeling and construction company serving Collegeville, PA and the surrounding Montgomery and Chester County area. With over 20 years of hands-on experience, Steve is known for quality craftsmanship, reliability, and attention to detail.

Steve began his career as a professional framer, constructing homes and residential developments for local builders. During this time, he developed a strong foundation in building systems, structural integrity, and the construction process. He later established Merman Construction Inc., focusing on exterior renovations, home additions, remodeling, and stucco remediation.

Over the past decade, Steve has received specialized training from industry leaders in diagnosing and repairing complex water intrusion and stucco-related issues, and is often called in after previous repairs have failed. This expertise allows him to accurately identify building failures and implement long-term repair solutions. Throughout his career, Steve has completed more than 1,000 residential projects and built experienced construction teams committed to high standards and client satisfaction.

Merman Construction Inc. is a locally owned and operated company based in Collegeville, PA and is committed to supporting animal rescue organizations, including City of Elderly Love Rescue and Speranza Animal Rescue. Craftsmanship, integrity, and community involvement remain central to every project.

Merman Construction Inc. is a trusted member of the Better Business Bureau for over 15 years. See our other trusted associations above.

Built on Planning and Precision

Merman Construction builds home additions that feel like they were always part of the original structure. We work with families throughout Plymouth Meeting and Montgomery County who love their location but have outgrown their space. Every addition we build is planned carefully, permitted correctly, and executed by Steve Merman and his crew from first day to final walkthrough.

 

Why Plymouth Meeting Homeowners Choose Us

Remodeling in Plymouth Meeting requires an understanding of homes built across several decades. Construction styles vary widely from postwar ranches near Germantown Pike to newer colonials in Whitemarsh Woods, and each era presents its own structural considerations. We work regularly in neighborhoods throughout Plymouth Township and understand the zoning setbacks, impervious coverage limits, and building codes required by Plymouth Township to keep your project on track and on budget.

What sets us apart is not just local knowledge, it is the level of personal involvement Steve brings to every job. He is not a salesman who hands your project off after signing. He is on site daily, managing the work, communicating with you directly, and ensuring the quality matches what was promised.

From Start to Finish

We plan every project carefully so the build is smooth, predictable, and respectful of your home and your schedule. That means thorough pre-construction planning to prevent surprises, clean and organized job sites throughout, clear communication at every stage, and a final walkthrough where nothing is considered done until you are satisfied.

 

Structural planning that prevents surprises
Clean job sites and clear communication
Quality materials installed correctly
Scheduling that respects your time

Home Additions
What We Build in Plymouth Meeting

From single story expansions to full second story additions, Merman Construction handles the complete scope of residential addition work throughout Plymouth Township. For detailed cost information visit our home additions page.

Single Story Additions: Open up kitchens, family rooms, or add flexible space.
In-Law Suites/ADUs: Independent living spaces for loved ones and guests.
Sunrooms/4-Season Rooms: Bright, insulated additions that bring in the outdoors.

 

Second Story Additions: Build upward without expanding your home’s footprint. These can be especially helpful when setbacks are in play.
Garage Conversions: Turn unused garages into high-function living space.
Bump-Out Expansions: Add space to kitchens, bathrooms, or nooks.
Home Addition

When you invest in a home addition, you’re opening up a world of possibilities. Whether you need more space for a growing family or simply want to increase your home’s value, a well-designed home addition can transform your living environment.

VIEW MORE
Bathroom Remodel

Kitchen and bathroom remodeling contractors can redefine your home, adding both functionality and aesthetic value. Whether you dream of a sleek, modern kitchen for culinary adventures or a luxurious bathroom retreat to unwind, a well-planned remodel can bring your vision to life and elevate your daily living.

VIEW MORE
Basement Renovation

A finished basement is one of the best ways to expand your home’s usable space and add long-term value. Instead of an unfinished storage or laundry area, your basement can become a welcoming extension of your home. Our team provides complete solutions: framing, insulation, electrical, and plumbing plus custom touches like wet bars, entertainment wiring, and modern lighting so the space feels as comfortable and efficient as the rest of the house.

Our Proven 5-Step Process

We make home additions simple, transparent, and stress-free from day one.

Consultation & Site Visit: We walk your property and define goals, scope, and style.
Design & Permits: We finalize your plans and handle local approvals and zoning.
Build Begins: Our team handles the foundation, framing, MEPs, and finishes.
Final Walkthrough: We handle inspections, punch list, and your final sign-off.
Warranty & Follow-Up: We stand behind our work and ensure long-term satisfaction.

Top ADU Contractors Near Me: 7 Reasons Las Vegas Homeowners Choose Greenso

Searching for adu contractors near me is the first step thousands of Las Vegas homeowners take every year — and for good reason. The Valley's housing market is tight, and a well-built accessory dwelling unit can solve two problems at once: adding living space and generating rental income.

Las Vegas is one of the fastest-growing cities in the U.S. In fact, Nevada's population grew by over 15% between 2010 and 2020, putting serious pressure on housing supply. As a result, more homeowners are turning their backyards into income-producing assets.

What Is an ADU and Why Las Vegas Homeowners Are Building Them

An accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is a secondary living space built on the same lot as your primary home. Simply put, it is a self-contained unit with its own entrance, kitchen, and bathroom — all on your existing residential lot.

ADUs go by many names in the Las Vegas Valley:

Granny flats or in-law suites
Casitas — very common in local culture
Garage conversions
Detached backyard cottages

Nevada has made it easier than ever to add a secondary unit. In fact, Nevada SB 150 loosened local zoning rules, pushing cities like Las Vegas to streamline ADU permits. Furthermore, according to Zillow Research, homes with ADUs sell for notably more than comparable properties without them.

Here are the top reasons homeowners are building ADUs right now:

Rental income — Las Vegas has a strong rental market, and a backyard unit can generate steady monthly cash flow.
Housing for family — Keep aging parents or adult children close without sacrificing privacy.
Property value boost — Adding livable square footage increases your home's resale appeal.
Short-term rentals — The tourism economy makes Las Vegas ideal for platforms like Airbnb.

Nevada homeowners may also qualify for energy-efficient ADU incentives through NV Energy's rebate programs, potentially reducing utility expenses meaningfully.

How to Find the Best ADU Contractors in Las Vegas

Finding the right local builder is the most important step in your project. The wrong hire can cost you time, money, and serious stress. The right one delivers a smooth build from permit to final walkthrough.

Start With Licensing and Insurance

Nevada law requires all general contractors to hold a valid state license. First, verify any contractor through the Nevada State Contractors Board. Also confirm they carry general liability insurance — robust coverage is a strong benchmark for projects of this size.

Key credentials to check:

Active Nevada contractor's license
General liability and workers' comp insurance
Specific ADU or home addition experience
Local Las Vegas project portfolio
Ask the Right Questions

Not every builder understands ADU-specific rules. For example, Las Vegas and Clark County have unique zoning codes, setback requirements, and utility hookup rules. A qualified ADU builder will know these details without hesitation.

Ask potential contractors:

How many ADUs have you built in Clark County?
Do you handle permits and inspections in-house?
Can you provide references from recent ADU clients?
What is your typical project timeline?

Moreover, check Google, Houzz, and the Better Business Bureau for consistent patterns — not just star ratings. In addition, ask to visit a completed project in person when possible.

Our guide on choosing the right ADU construction contractor in Las Vegas goes deeper on red flags to avoid. You can also explore our ADU construction services to understand what a thorough proposal should include.

The ADU Construction Process Step by Step

Building an ADU moves through several clear phases. Each step builds on the last, so knowing what to expect helps you stay on schedule and avoid costly surprises.

Phase 1: Design and Planning. First, you'll work with your contractor to define the project scope. This includes choosing the ADU type, setting a layout, and confirming the build fits your lot. In Las Vegas, Clark County requires a site plan, floor plan, and elevation drawings before any permit is issued.

Key planning tasks include:

Lot size and setback review
Utility connection assessment
HOA approval (if applicable)
Architectural drawing preparation

Phase 2: Permitting. Next, your contractor submits drawings to Clark County Development Services. Permit review typically takes 4 to 8 weeks, depending on project complexity. However, incomplete applications can push that timeline out significantly.

Phase 3: Site Preparation and Foundation. Once permits are approved, ground work begins. This covers grading, excavation, and pouring the foundation. In Nevada's desert climate, soil conditions vary widely, so a proper foundation inspection is critical.

Phase 4: Framing, Mechanical, and Exterior. Framing goes up first, followed by electrical, plumbing, and HVAC rough-ins. Exterior sheathing, roofing, and stucco are completed next. Each trade requires a separate inspection before the next phase starts.

Phase 5: Interior Finishes and Final Inspection. Finally, drywall, flooring, cabinetry, and fixtures are installed. Your contractor then schedules a final inspection with the county. After passing, you receive a Certificate of Occupancy. The full timeline from design to move-in typically runs 4 to 9 months.

Our ADU construction service page outlines what a full-service build includes from start to finish.

ADU Types and What Each Costs in Las Vegas

Las Vegas homeowners have several ADU styles to choose from. Each type fits a different lot size, budget, and goal. Understanding your options helps you plan smarter from day one.

Detached ADUs are fully separate structures built in your backyard. They offer the most privacy and flexibility. However, they also tend to fall in the upper-tier to premium-tier range because of foundation, utility hookups, and full exterior construction requirements. These are best for long-term rentals, multigenerational living, or maximizing resale value.

Attached ADUs share one wall with your main home. Because they use an existing structure, construction is simpler. As a result, pricing typically lands in the mid-tier to upper-tier range, depending on size and finishes.

Garage Conversions are one of the most popular ADU builds in Las Vegas. Many homeowners already have a two-car garage with unused square footage. Costs are generally entry-tier to mid-tier, making this the most budget-friendly path. Additionally, garage conversions benefit from lower foundation costs, existing roof and walls, and faster permit approval in many cases.

Junior ADUs (JADUs) are carved out of existing interior space — often a bedroom or bonus room. Nevada law allows JADUs up to 500 square feet. Specifically, these are the most affordable option, typically entry-tier to standard-tier.

Detached ADU	High	High	6–9 months	Rental income, full independence
Attached ADU	Medium	Medium	4–7 months	Family housing, resale value
Garage Conversion	Medium	Low–Medium	3–6 months	Budget-friendly, fastest path
Junior ADU (JADU)	Low	Low	2–4 months	Affordable, interior repurpose
Above-Garage ADU	High	Medium–High	5–8 months	Small lots, urban infill

About Alison

My love of home construction started in elementary school, when my Father designed and built our passive solar home during the energy crisis of the 1970’s.  I was part of his crew and by high school, was using power tools to rough frame walls and roofs with Habitat for Humanity.

After earning a Bachelors Degree in International Relations at Mount Holyoke College, and spending two years in the theater’s costume shop, I chose to pursue my love of clothing design and earned an Associates Degree from the Fashion Institute of Technology in New York City.

For the next decade, I worked as a textile designer at companies such as Gap Inc. and home furnishing textile manufacturers.

My first home, a 1918 Arts & Crafts Colonial, shifted my course once again.  In 2004 I embarked on my second career as a Kitchen and Bath Designer, which melded all of my loves together into one career.  

After working for nearly a decade at Canterbury Design Kitchen Interiors, a premier kitchen design studio in Morristown, NJ, I founded Griffin Designs Kitchen & Bath in 2018.

A Local Remodeling Company Built Around Accountability

A local remodeling company and general contractor serving homeowners across Northern Virginia, Fredericksburg, Maryland and Washington, DC.

OUR STORY

Built around planning, not guesswork

Virginia Pro Remodel was formed around a simple idea: remodeling projects go better when design and construction are handled by one accountable team instead of being split between separate companies who never talk to each other directly.

We work with homeowners across Northern Virginia, the Fredericksburg region, Maryland and Washington, DC on kitchens, bathrooms, basements, additions and whole-home renovations. Every project starts with the same questions: how do you actually use the space, what is not working, and what would make it work.

From there, our team develops a layout, confirms it against the structure and systems already in the house, and documents the scope before any wall comes down. That sequence is not extra process for its own sake — it is what keeps a schedule and a budget realistic once construction starts.

HOW WE WORK

What it means to work with one team

One contractor plans your project, pulls the permits and builds it — no handoffs between companies.

In a traditional model, homeowners hire a designer or architect first, then separately hire a contractor to build what was drawn. If the design turns out to be over budget or difficult to build, the homeowner is stuck coordinating changes between two companies who were not in the room together.

The same team develops the layout, selects materials with real availability and cost in mind, prepares permit drawings, and then builds the project. Constructability and budget are part of the conversation from the first meeting, not a surprise after the drawings are finished.

WHY IT MATTERS TO YOU

One point of contact and one contract for design and construction
Decisions get made once, not renegotiated between companies
Selections are checked against the budget before you commit
Permit drawings reflect what can actually be built

Advance Design’s Roots Go Deep

Advance Design Studio Building circa 2002

Advance Design Studio’s founding family has been a cornerstone of the Gilberts, Illinois, community since the early 1900s, with their business roots stretching across twelve decades in the same building at 30 Railroad Street. Originally established in 1992 as Advance Builders, Inc., the company began by specializing in kitchen and bath remodeling, residential renovations, and new home construction throughout the Northwest suburbs of Chicago.

In 2002, the business expanded its offerings to include professional design services, leading to the launch of Advance Design Studio, Ltd. The rebranded company provided a more comprehensive approach to home remodeling, combining in-house design with a full-service showroom featuring cabinetry, countertops, tile, plumbing fixtures, and lighting. This integration of design and construction allowed the company to offer clients a seamless, all-in-one remodeling experience from initial concept to finished project.

Today, Advance Design Studio continues to thrive in its original location, with a spacious 3,500 square-foot showroom and design hub that serves as the heart of the company. The building remains a prominent feature of Gilberts, nestled between the local firehouse and post office, and the company is proud to maintain its deep connection to the community.

Throughout its growth, the company has remained steadfast in its mission to deliver high-quality craftsmanship and client-focused service. Since 2009, it has been recognized by Remodeling Magazine as one of the nation’s Top 500 Remodeling Companies, consistently ranking among the top 50 design/build firms. This recognition reflects the company’s commitment to excellence and its reputation as a trusted leader in the industry.

Locally, Advance Design Studio continues to be a pillar of the local community, known for its dedication to making the remodeling process as seamless, convenient, and rewarding as possible for every client. With a focus on customer satisfaction and a comprehensive, integrated approach to home remodeling, the company has earned the trust and loyalty of generations of homeowners.

	

With the Common-Sense Remodeling process, you can have a fully customized, predictable, and positive remodeling experience free from the headaches of traditional remodeling.

Back It

Our Story
WL Kitchen & Home was founded in 1988 by husband and wife team Gabriel Salazar, and Olga Botero who opened a small shop in Lodi, New Jersey to design and build custom cabinetry.

Upon the arrival of architect Julio Botero, their line of work was expanded to include architectural interiors such as libraries, theaters, closets & bathrooms, and wine cellars.

Their mission has always been to create beautifully handcrafted pieces for their clients. This has resulted in WL Kitchen & Home attaining a devoted following of loyal customers, all of which share their values in regards to both quality and craftsmanship.

Bathroom Renovation Timeline in Contra Costa County: What Homeowners Should Expect

Bathroom Renovation Timeline in Contra Costa County: What Homeowners Should Expect

Planning a bathroom renovation is exciting—until you start wondering how long your bathroom will actually be out of service.

Will the project take a couple of weeks? A month? Longer?

The answer depends on the size of the bathroom, the scope of the renovation, the materials you choose, whether plumbing or electrical work is required, and whether permits and inspections are involved.

For homeowners in Contra Costa County, the permitting and inspection process can also be an important part of the timeline. The County identifies bathroom remodeling as work that generally requires a building permit, with requirements varying based on the project’s scope.

A straightforward bathroom update may move relatively quickly, while a renovation involving layout changes, relocated fixtures, new plumbing, electrical work or structural modifications can take considerably longer.

This guide explains the typical stages of a bathroom renovation in Contra Costa County so you know what to expect before construction begins.

How Long Does a Bathroom Renovation Take?

There isn’t one standard timeline for every bathroom renovation.

A simple like-for-like update may take considerably less time than a complete bathroom renovation involving demolition, plumbing changes, electrical work, new flooring, shower construction, cabinetry and multiple inspections.

For planning purposes, think of your bathroom renovation as a series of stages rather than one continuous block of construction:

Initial planning and consultation
Design and project scope
Material selection
Permit preparation and approval
Demolition
Plumbing and electrical work
Walls and waterproofing
Flooring, tile and shower installation
Vanity, fixtures and accessories
Final inspection and completion

Some of these stages overlap, while others cannot begin until earlier work has been completed or inspected.

The exact timeline can change depending on your bathroom and the scope of work.

Stage 1: Planning Your Bathroom Renovation
Start With What Isn’t Working

Before choosing tile colors or looking at vanities, identify the problems you want the renovation to solve.

Is the bathroom too small?

Do you need more storage?

Is the shower difficult to use?

Are the fixtures outdated?

Does the lighting need improvement?

Does the current layout waste space?

These questions help determine whether you’re looking at a cosmetic update or a more comprehensive renovation.

A clear project scope at the beginning can prevent unnecessary changes later.

Stage 2: Design and Layout Planning

Once you know what you want to improve, the next step is developing the design.

This is where you decide on:

Bathroom layout
Vanity size
Shower or bathtub configuration
Toilet placement
Storage
Lighting
Flooring
Wall tile
Shower tile
Faucets
Fixtures
Mirrors
Finishes
Do You Need to Change the Bathroom Layout?

This is one of the most important decisions affecting the timeline.

If your existing plumbing and fixtures stay in approximately the same locations, the project may be simpler.

If you move the shower, toilet, sink or bathtub, additional plumbing and construction work may be required.

Contra Costa County’s residential bathroom remodel requirements specifically call for plans showing existing and proposed conditions when fixtures are relocated or the bathroom size changes.

That’s why layout decisions should be made early—not after construction has already started.

Stage 3: Choosing Your Bathroom Materials

Material selection is another part of the timeline that homeowners sometimes underestimate.

Before construction begins, you’ll want to have decisions made about major materials and fixtures such as:

Tile
Vanity
Countertop
Shower fixtures
Bathtub
Toilet
Faucets
Mirrors
Lighting
Flooring
Cabinet hardware
Shower enclosure
Why Does Material Selection Affect the Timeline?

Because your contractor can’t install materials that haven’t arrived.

If a particular vanity, tile or fixture is delayed, the installation schedule may have to change.

For this reason, it’s smart to make major selections early and confirm product availability before the project starts.

Stage 4: Permits and Approvals in Contra Costa County

Permits are an important part of planning a bathroom renovation in Contra Costa County.

The County’s home improvement guidance identifies bathroom remodeling as work that generally requires a building permit, although exact requirements depend on the scope of the project.

For bathroom remodels, the County’s published requirements indicate that plans may be needed when fixtures are relocated or the bathroom size changes.

How Long Can the Permit Process Take?

Contra Costa County says its building plan check process generally takes two to four weeks, although the actual processing time depends on the type and complexity of the project. The County also notes that applications must be complete before plan review can proceed efficiently.

That means homeowners shouldn’t assume that permit approval will happen immediately.

A complete application, accurate plans and timely responses to plan-review comments can help keep the process moving.

Stage 5: Bathroom Demolition

Once the necessary approvals are in place and the project is ready to begin, demolition can start.

Depending on the renovation, this may involve removing:

Existing tile
Flooring
Vanity
Toilet
Tub
Shower components
Cabinets
Fixtures
Wall materials

Demolition is more than simply making the bathroom look empty.

It gives the remodeling team an opportunity to see what’s behind the existing finishes.

What If Something Unexpected Is Found?

This is one reason a bathroom renovation timeline should always have some flexibility.

Once walls, flooring or other materials are removed, the project may reveal conditions that were not visible during the initial planning stage.

For example, there may be unexpected plumbing issues, damaged materials or conditions that require additional work.

When this happens, the timeline can change.

Stage 6: Plumbing and Electrical Work

After demolition, behind-the-wall work can begin.

This may include:

Plumbing modifications
New water lines
Drain adjustments
Shower valve installation
Electrical wiring
New outlets
Lighting connections
Exhaust fan work

This stage is particularly important because much of the work will eventually be hidden behind walls.

Contra Costa County’s bathroom remodel guidance identifies rough plumbing and electrical inspections that should take place before wallboard is installed when applicable.

Why Can’t This Work Simply Be Covered Immediately?

Because required inspections need to happen at the appropriate stage.

Covering walls before the necessary rough inspections can create problems and potentially require work to be opened again.

Stage 7: Waterproofing the Shower and Wet Areas

Waterproofing is one of the most important parts of a bathroom renovation.

The finished tile may be what everyone notices, but the layers behind that tile are critical to protecting the bathroom from moisture.

Depending on the project, this stage can include:

Shower waterproofing
Shower pan preparation
Underlayment
Drain installation
Water testing where required

Contra Costa County’s bathroom remodel requirements include inspections related to underlayment and shower pan testing when applicable.

Don’t Rush This Stage

A beautiful tile installation cannot compensate for poor waterproofing.

The goal is to create a bathroom that looks good and performs properly for years to come.

Stage 8: Tile and Flooring Installation

Once the underlying work is ready, the visible transformation starts to happen.

Tile may be installed on:

Shower walls
Shower floors
Bathroom walls
Bathroom floors
Backsplash areas

The timeline can vary depending on the size and complexity of the tile design.

Large-format tile, intricate patterns, multiple tile types or custom layouts may require more planning and installation time than a straightforward design.

Stage 9: Vanity, Countertop and Storage Installation

After major tile and flooring work is completed, the bathroom begins to come together.

This stage may include installing:

Vanity
Cabinets
Countertop
Sink
Medicine cabinet
Shelving
Storage accessories
Plan Storage Before This Stage

If storage wasn’t considered during the initial design, it can be difficult to add meaningful storage later.

Think about what you actually need to store:

Towels
Toiletries
Hair-care products
Cleaning supplies
Personal-care items
Everyday bathroom essentials

A well-designed vanity can make a bathroom feel considerably more organized.

Stage 10: Fixtures, Mirrors and Lighting

Now the finishing elements are installed.

This may include:

Faucets
Shower fixtures
Toilet
Tub fixtures
Mirrors
Light fixtures
Exhaust fan
Towel bars
Toilet paper holder
Shower accessories
Cabinet hardware

At this stage, the bathroom starts to look much closer to the original design.

Stage 11: Final Inspection and Walkthrough

Once the renovation is complete, required final inspections can be scheduled.

Contra Costa County explains that inspections are used to verify that the completed work meets the permitted plans.

The County’s bathroom remodel guide states that the final inspection should take place after all work has been completed.

After the required inspections are completed, the final step is a walkthrough to identify any remaining touch-ups or adjustments.

What Can Make a Bathroom Renovation Take Longer?

Even a well-planned renovation can encounter delays.

Here are some of the most common factors.

Permit or Plan Review Delays

If plans need corrections or additional information, the review process can take longer.

Contra Costa County notes that plan review can involve multiple rounds of communication and revisions depending on the application.

Material Delays

A missing vanity, tile shipment or fixture can prevent the next stage from moving forward.

Layout Changes

Moving plumbing or changing the bathroom configuration can add construction work.

Unexpected Conditions

Demolition can reveal issues that were not visible beforehand.

Design Changes During Construction

Changing your mind after materials have been ordered or installed can affect both schedule and cost.

Inspection Scheduling

Required inspections need to occur at the appropriate stages before certain work can be covered or completed.

How to Make Your Bathroom Remodel Go More Smoothly

You can’t eliminate every possible delay, but good preparation can make a major difference.

1. Finalize Your Layout Early

Don’t wait until construction begins to decide where your shower, vanity or toilet should go.

2. Select Materials Before Work Starts

Choose your major finishes and fixtures early and confirm availability.

3. Understand Your Permit Requirements

Don’t assume every bathroom project follows the same process.

Contra Costa County provides specific bathroom remodel requirements and recommends determining permit requirements before beginning work.

4. Keep Your Priorities Clear

Know which improvements are essential and which ones are optional.

5. Leave Some Flexibility in Your Schedule

A renovation timeline is an estimate, not a guarantee.

Unexpected conditions can happen, especially once existing materials are removed.

Should You Stay Home During a Bathroom Renovation?

That depends on your household and the scope of the project.

For a small bathroom update, living at home may be relatively manageable.

For a major renovation, however, you’ll need to consider:

How many bathrooms your home has
Whether another bathroom is available
How much construction noise you can tolerate
Dust and debris
Access to the work area
Children or pets
How long the bathroom will be unavailable

If you’re remodeling your only bathroom, discuss the expected schedule and daily access with your remodeling team before work begins.

How to Plan Around Your Bathroom Remodeling Timeline

A little preparation can make the renovation much easier on your household.

Before construction starts:

Choose your materials.

Don’t leave major decisions until installation week.

Create a temporary bathroom routine.

If you have another bathroom, decide how your household will use it while the renovation is underway.

Move personal items out of the bathroom.

Pack toiletries, towels and other belongings before demolition.

Protect nearby areas.

Construction traffic can affect hallways, floors and adjacent rooms, so discuss protection measures with your remodeling team.

Keep communication open.

Ask for updates when major stages are completed and discuss any changes before making decisions.

When Is the Best Time to Start a Bathroom Renovation in Contra Costa County?

There’s no single perfect season for every bathroom renovation.

The best time depends on your household schedule, project scope, material availability and contractor scheduling.

If you have a specific deadline—such as preparing your home for guests, completing another renovation or getting ready to sell—start the planning process well in advance.

Remember that the project timeline begins before demolition.

Design, material selection, permitting and scheduling can all happen before the first tile is removed.

Planning a Bathroom Renovation in Contra Costa County?

A bathroom renovation doesn’t have to feel overwhelming.

The key is understanding that the project is made up of several connected stages. When planning, design, materials, construction and inspections are coordinated from the beginning, you have a much clearer picture of what to expect.

If you’re considering a bathroom renovation in Contra Costa County, Projat Solutions can help you plan your project around your goals, space and desired improvements.

Whether you’re updating an outdated bathroom or planning a more complete transformation, start by defining what you want the finished space to accomplish.

Contact Projat Solutions to discuss your bathroom renovation plans and take the next step toward creating a bathroom that works better for your home.

Final Thoughts

A bathroom renovation timeline is about more than the number of days workers spend inside the bathroom.

The project starts with planning, continues through design and material selection, moves into permitting and construction, and ends with inspections and final details.

For Contra Costa County homeowners, understanding the local permit and inspection process is particularly important. The County provides specific requirements for bathroom remodels, including inspections at key stages of applicable projects.

The better prepared you are before construction begins, the easier it is to manage expectations and keep the project moving.

If you’re considering a bathroom renovation, focus first on what you want to improve, how you want the space to function and what matters most to your household. Then build the project timeline around those priorities.

A well-planned renovation can give you a bathroom that isn’t just newer—it can be more comfortable, functional and enjoyable to use every day.

Frequently asked questions
General
Is the estimate free?

Yes! We offer free estimates and in-home consultations. But that’s not all—our team goes the extra mile. We provide free advice, visit suppliers with you, gather pricing information, and ensure you have all the details you need to make informed decisions about your remodeling project.

Are you licensed contractor?

Yes, we are a fully licensed contractor in Washington State (License #KITCHKB763OR). Additionally, every specialist we work with, whether a plumber, electrician, or HVAC technician, is licensed. If your project requires an architect or engineer, we can connect you with trusted professionals. Our goal is to ensure your remodel not only looks stunning but also complies with all regulations.

How soon can you start?

Once all materials are on-site, we can typically begin your project within a few days.

How long will the remodel take?

The timeline depends on the scope of your project. Generally:

Bathroom remodels take about 3-4 weeks.

Kitchen remodels are completed in 2-4 weeks.

Flooring installations typically take 1-5 days.

How to save money on my kitchen/bathroom remodel?

The key is open communication about your options. Every material and installed item comes with its own cost, and we’re here to help you navigate those choices. By discussing your needs and budget, we can work together to find alternatives and solutions that make your remodel both beautiful and affordable.

Who will buy the materials?

We handle the purchase of construction and consumable materials like drywall, mud, paint, tile backer, framing wood, plumbing pipes, fittings, and cables. For finishing materials such as tile, vanities, cabinets, and lights, we can either install items you’ve purchased or buy them on your behalf—whichever suits you best. We’ll discuss all options to ensure we install exactly what you want and what works for your space.

Why Consider a Second Story Addition?

Adding a second story to your home offers numerous advantages:

Increased Living Space: A second story addition provides additional square footage to accommodate growing families, creating extra bedrooms, bathrooms, or versatile spaces like offices or playrooms.
Improved Property Value: Homes with well-planned second-story additions can see a significant increase in market value. If you plan to sell in the future, this improvement can yield a high return on investment.
Enhanced Comfort and Functionality: With a second story, you can separate living areas and create more private spaces, enhancing overall comfort.
Beautiful Views: A second story addition can offer stunning views of your neighborhood or the surrounding landscape, allowing you to experience your home in a new light.
Avoiding the Cost of Moving: Instead of searching for a new home and incurring costs like closing fees and moving expenses, a second story addition allows you to optimize your existing space.

We keep you in the loop. From the first walkthrough to the final day, we communicate clearly, listen to your needs, and work with you as part of the team.

	Caring, Problem-Solving Approach

Remodeling always comes with surprises. We think ahead, stay flexible, and find solutions when challenges come up — with a focus on moving forward.

	Craftsmanship & Dedication

We build with care and commitment. We focus on doing things right, pay attention to the details, and make sure your home is built to last.

How Your Project Comes to Life—Step by Step

We understand that your home is personal, and starting a remodel is a big decision. That’s why we begin by listening—taking the time to understand your needs, goals, and how you live your day-to-day life. From there, we keep the process clear, communicate along the way, and focus on delivering results. Get in touch with us today!

Contact Us

Tell us a bit about your project using our contact form. Upload a few photos of the proposed work area so we can understand your goals and scope. Then we’ll schedule an initial call to see how we can best help.

Project Evaluation

If we can help, we’ll schedule an on-site evaluation. From there, we’ll plan the next step; this may include design work, a detailed scope, and an estimate and proposal before any work begins.

Project Construction

With the plan finalized and approvals in place, we begin the construction. We’ll keep you updated, answer your questions, and make sure everything stays on track from start to finish.

Enjoy Your New Space

Now the fun part: using your new space. Whether it’s a better layout, new finishes, or just more comfort, we hope it brings you and your family years of enjoyment.

About Us
Our Story

Edgar got his first taste of carpentry as a kid, helping his dad, who was a carpenter. That’s where he learned the value of hard work, respect for the trades, and the importance of family values.

He started working in construction at 21, learning the trades hands-on with local contractors across the Bay Area while also taking classes at a community college to deepen his knowledge. Over time, he built his skills and experience in residential construction.

Eventually, Edgar saw an opportunity to go out on his own, combining his experience with a more effective customer service approach for homeowners. That’s how PointVertex began: out of a dream, a strong work ethic, and the drive to build something better.

Today, Edgar stays involved in every job. His values are simple: faith, family, respect for people, and pride in the trades. PointVertex is built on those values and takes pride in delivering a high-quality finished product and improving the lives of the people it serves.

Outside of work, Edgar enjoys spending time with family, mountain biking, working out, and firing up the grill on weekends. The same steady, friendly energy he brings to life shows up in every project.

Our Mission

We enrich our clients’ lives by transforming their homes into safe, functional spaces that reflect their vision, support family moments, and create lasting memories. With attentive service and quality craftsmanship, we enhance comfort, value, and overall well‑being.

We service the following areas:

​Oakland, Alameda, San Leandro, San Lorenzo, Hayward, Union City, Fremont, Pleasanton, Livermore, San Ramon, Denville, Alamo, Lafayette, Orinda, Moraga, Montclair, Piedmont, Emeryville, Albany, Berkeley, Walnut Creek, Pleasant Hill.​

MEET THE FOUNDER: TAYLOR SORENSON

Hello, Utah! I’m Taylor Sorenson, President and Founder of Utah Home Remodel Experts.

As a Salt Lake County native, construction has always been part of my story. I grew up surrounded by the sounds of hammers, saws, and hardworking hands—my grandfather, father, and uncles all helped build and maintain the communities that make Utah home. From an early age, they brought me along to job sites, teaching not just skills, but the deeper values behind them: craftsmanship, integrity, and pride in work done well.

Family and a strong work ethic remain at the heart of everything I do. Utah Home Remodel Experts was built on that legacy—a commitment to honest work, lasting quality, and treating every home we remodel with the same care we’d give our own.

OUR TEAM: YOUR PROJECT IS OUR PROJECT

Behind every successful remodel is a team that cares as much about your home as you do. At Utah Home Remodel Experts, we’ve built a crew that shares the same values Taylor grew up with—integrity, craftsmanship, and respect for every homeowner we serve.

We know how frustrating it can be to start a project with big hopes, only to have timelines slip and costs climb. That’s not how we do business. From the start, our team takes the time to truly listen—understanding your goals, your budget, and how you want your space to feel. Then we plan, price, and schedule every phase before construction begins, so you’ll know exactly what to expect from beginning to end.

Every project, whether a single-room update or a full-home transformation, receives the same attention to detail and quality we’d demand in our own homes. With our client-first approach, experienced craftsmanship, and commitment to surprise-free results, we’re here to make your remodel not just successful—but genuinely enjoyable.

Written by Rohrer for Construction | Serving Lake County, IL since 1989 —
Last reviewed/Updated: October 2026
Add living space above your existing home

A second-story addition adds a new floor over some or all of a home’s existing footprint. Unlike a ground-level expansion, it can provide substantial new living space without extending the house into the yard. The scope may include removing the existing roof, structural reinforcement, new exterior walls and roofing, stairs, windows, insulation, interior finishes, and updates to heating, cooling, electrical, or plumbing systems.

The layout depends on how you want the home to work. Some homeowners prioritize bedrooms and a bathroom; others need a quiet office, guest space, or a family room upstairs. We help connect those needs to a practical plan and coordinate the addition with the rest of the home. Explore our home addition services to compare project types.

New bedrooms, a primary suite, or additional bathrooms
A home office, flexible bonus room, or expanded family space
Stair placement and circulation planned around the existing floor plan
Exterior details selected to complement the original house
Check the structure, layout, and materials first

Before choosing finishes, the home needs a feasibility review. The existing foundation, load-bearing walls, framing, and roof structure all affect what can be added and how the work must be supported. A structural professional may need to assess the house and provide engineering plans. The proposed footprint and height also need to fit applicable zoning and setback rules.

Many Lake County homes are 1950s–1990s ranches, split-levels, and colonials, and each type presents different planning questions. A ranch may need a carefully located new staircase and a plan for how the old roof will be replaced. A split-level may require more attention to transitions between floors. For any home, the new rooms should feel connected to the existing layout rather than like an isolated upper floor.

Material choices influence the exterior appearance and interior comfort. Siding, trim, roofing, and window styles can be selected to relate to the existing facade, while interior flooring, doors, and finishes can match or intentionally distinguish the new rooms. Lake County’s freeze-thaw winters make sound detailing around roofing, windows, and exterior joints important. Insulation and heating and cooling plans should also account for the added space and the home’s existing systems.

What happens during a second-story addition

A vertical addition is a major construction project, so planning includes more than drawing new rooms. Work may affect access to the existing home, protection from weather while the roof is open, and how household systems serve the new floor. The scope and sequence are developed around the approved plans and the conditions found at the property.

Rohrer manages the construction process and coordinates the trades involved in the work. We also handle permits, which can involve both local building review and zoning requirements. Requirements differ by jurisdiction, so we confirm which rules apply to your property instead of assuming one village’s process covers another. Our building permit guidance explains why permit coordination belongs in project planning.

Roof removal and temporary weather protection as the structure is opened
Structural framing and connections to the existing home
Installation of the new roof, exterior walls, windows, and insulation
Interior construction, finishes, and necessary system extensions

Why Permits and Inspections Are Important

Building permits and inspections are crucial for homeowners planning any construction or home remodeling in Lake County. Permits ensure compliance with building codes and safety standards, protecting your investment. Unpermitted work can lead to fines, legal complications, or issues with resale.

Permit Authorities: Lake County vs. City or Township

Depending on your location, the authority responsible for issuing permits will vary. If you’re in an incorporated village or city, your local government—such as Grayslake or Gurnee—handles your permit. If you’re in an unincorporated area, the Lake County Planning, Building & Development Department is your go-to office.

Unsure about your jurisdiction? Always confirm with your township or city hall. Contact us if you need help identifying the right authority.

Why Homeowners Look at Financing Before Remodeling

Most remodeling decisions are not just about appearance. In many homes, the real reason is function. A kitchen may feel cramped or outdated. A bathroom may be worn down or no longer practical. A basement may be unfinished while more living space is badly needed. Exterior issues may be getting pushed off even though they are not going away.

Financing often comes into the picture when the project makes sense, but paying the full cost out of pocket all at once does not. It can create room to move forward sooner, especially when the work improves daily living, solves an ongoing issue, or prevents a problem from getting worse.

Important to know: Rohrer for Construction does not offer in-house financing. Any financing explored through RenoFi is separate and depends on qualification, lender approval, and available loan terms.

Before applying for anything, it helps to understand the likely scope of the work, the rough cost range, and what parts of the project matter most.

Common Financing Options for a Home Remodel

There is no perfect financing option for everyone. The right fit depends on the size of the project, how much equity is available, how quickly funding is needed, and how the monthly payment fits into the rest of the household budget.

RenoFi renovation financing

RenoFi may be worth exploring for homeowners planning a meaningful remodel and looking for a financing path built around renovation work. This option may be especially relevant when the project is larger and the homeowner wants to evaluate financing based on the renovation itself.

Because Rohrer for Construction does not provide in-house financing, RenoFi is offered as a separate financing partner for qualifying homeowners.

Explore RenoFi

Home equity loans and HELOCs

These are common for homeowners who have built equity and want to use it toward a remodel. A home equity loan usually provides a fixed lump sum, while a HELOC works more like a line of credit that can be used as needed.

These options often come up for medium to larger projects such as kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, basement finishing, and additions.

Personal loans

Personal loans can be a practical option for smaller or more contained projects. They may move faster than equity-based financing and do not always require the same level of home value or equity.

For homeowners doing a smaller bathroom update, a limited kitchen refresh, or targeted repair-and-upgrade work, this can be one of the first options worth comparing.

FHA Title I loans

Some homeowners also look into FHA Title I home improvement loans, especially when available equity is limited. These can sometimes be worth researching when the goal is to improve the home but traditional equity-based borrowing is not the right fit.

Like any program-based financing option, terms and eligibility should be reviewed carefully.

Credit card promotions or short-term financing

For smaller purchases, appliances, or limited-scope work, promotional financing may sometimes be part of the conversation. But this is also where homeowners can get burned if the terms are not understood clearly.

Deferred interest, payment deadlines, and rate changes should all be reviewed before going down this path.

Cash plus partial financing

Some homeowners choose to combine savings with financing instead of borrowing the entire project cost. That can be a smart middle-ground option when there is enough cash to cover part of the work but not enough to comfortably handle everything.

This approach can also help keep payments smaller while still allowing the project to move forward.

RenoFi vs HELOC vs Personal Loan

Each financing path comes with tradeoffs. This quick comparison can help narrow down which option may deserve a closer look.

Option	Often Best For	What to Watch
RenoFi	Larger remodels where renovation-focused financing may make more sense	Qualification, lender approval, and actual loan terms still vary
HELOC	Homeowners with solid equity who want flexible access to funds	Variable rates and changing payment amounts can matter
Home Equity Loan	Projects where a fixed amount and fixed payment are preferred	Requires available equity and is less flexible once funds are issued
Personal Loan	Smaller remodels or projects where speed and simplicity matter	Rates may be higher than equity-based options depending on profile
Cash + Financing	Homeowners who want to reduce how much they borrow	Still requires clear planning so the project does not outgrow the budget
Real Remodeling Financing Scenarios in Lake County, IL

Homeowners in Lake County towns like Gurnee, Libertyville, Grayslake, Round Lake, Antioch, Vernon Hills, Waukegan, and Lindenhurst often run into the same question: is it better to wait and save more, or move ahead now with financing?

The answer usually depends on the project and the reason behind it. A small cosmetic refresh is one thing. A kitchen that no longer works, a bathroom that needs updating, or a basement that could solve a space problem is another.

01
Example: A kitchen remodel around $45,000 to $70,000

For a homeowner planning a larger kitchen remodel, financing may make sense when the goal is to improve layout, storage, and daily function now instead of dragging the project out over several years.

02
Example: A bathroom remodel around $15,000 to $30,000

For a bathroom that is worn out, dated, or becoming harder to use, a personal loan or smaller financing path may be worth comparing depending on the scope of the work and available equity.

03
Example: A basement finish or multi-room project

For a larger basement renovation or broader remodel, understanding the Basement Renovation Cost Guide for Lake County Homeowners and exploring renovation-focused financing may be more relevant when the project is intended to create meaningful living space and improve long-term use of the home.

How to Choose the Right Financing Path

The best financing choice is not just about approval. It is about choosing something that fits the project and still feels manageable afterward.

The size and complexity of the remodel
Whether the work needs to happen now or can wait
How much home equity is available
Whether fixed or variable payments feel more comfortable
How fast funding is needed
How the payment fits within the household budget
Whether the project is improving function, value, or both

The goal is not to borrow the most. The goal is to choose a path that makes sense for the home and the household.

Why Getting Clear on Scope First Helps

Financing decisions usually go better when the project itself is better defined. That is why many homeowners start with scope before they start with loan paperwork.

It keeps the project more realistic from the start
It helps avoid building a budget around guesses
It reduces the chance of major scope changes mid-project
It makes estimate conversations more productive
It helps identify what matters most if priorities need to be trimmed

If the project still feels blurry, the Home Remodel Scope Builder can help organize ideas before moving into pricing or financing.
